blocks.text:
# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # regresses here, not only on the runner.

    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage

  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs

  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

blocks.text:
# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # regresses here, not only on the runner.

    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]

Solid, well-tested implementation of the gh-1589 contract: `Session.seal()` (per-instance writer state, no file-format change), the `_reactionRunsSealed` fence on every headless terminal path, the drain → usage fold → board/ledger flushes → seal close order in both `runHeadless`' finally and `_teardownAfterRepl` (REG-2), and the adapter's terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded reap → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm, loud AC7 degradation) on the ladder, wait_for-cancel, no-knobs, and external-cap-only paths. Verified locally: `dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart` (13 ✅), the drain/liveness (10 ✅) and task-tool (45 ✅) regression files, `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` (222 ✅), and `dart analyze` clean on all changed files.

## Key Issues

- ⚠️ **Ticket test-plan gap (documented deferral, but half of it is not tiered as follow-up in the ticket):** REG-1/REG-2 as *standalone merge-blocking CI jobs* (the ticket's explicit merge rule) and IT-4 (seal → resume → replay+repair → registry terminal-only rebuild) are not delivered; REG-1's essence is embedded as in-test watchdog assertions and REG-2 as one REPL test, which mitigates but does not satisfy the merge-rule wording. UT-4 (torn-tail repair) also has no new test — low risk since `session_repair.dart` is untouched and already covered by `test/session/session_repair_test.dart`, but the matrix lists it.
- ⚠️ Late-write sink is not guarded: a throwing `onLateWrite` sink would propagate into the late-write caller, weakening I1's "never thrown into an unhandled zone" (see inline comment on `_sealSessionForExit`).
- 💡 `_reactionRunsSealed` is never reset (latent trap only — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` runs headless exactly once per process and `exit()` follows; see inline comment).
- 💡 Formatting: new test files (and one hunk in `agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) are not `dart format`-clean (see inline comment). No CI format gate exists and the pre-commit hook self-heals, so this is cosmetic.

## Next Steps

1. Land the follow-up card for the REG-1/REG-2 standalone CI jobs + IT-4 + E2E legs before the next TB harness bump, or amend the ticket's merge rule to match the embedded-watchdog reality.
2. Consider wrapping the seal sink call in try/catch so I1's no-throw guarantee holds regardless of sink health.

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

Solid, well-tested implementation of the gh-1589 contract: `Session.seal()` (per-instance writer state, no file-format change), the `_reactionRunsSealed` fence on every headless terminal path, the drain → usage fold → board/ledger flushes → seal close order in both `runHeadless`' finally and `_teardownAfterRepl` (REG-2), and the adapter's terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded reap → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm, loud AC7 degradation) on the ladder, wait_for-cancel, no-knobs, and external-cap-only paths. Verified locally: `dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart` (13 ✅), the drain/liveness (10 ✅) and task-tool (45 ✅) regression files, `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` (222 ✅), and `dart analyze` clean on all changed files.

## Key Issues

- ⚠️ **Ticket test-plan gap (documented deferral, but half of it is not tiered as follow-up in the ticket):** REG-1/REG-2 as *standalone merge-blocking CI jobs* (the ticket's explicit merge rule) and IT-4 (seal → resume → replay+repair → registry terminal-only rebuild) are not delivered; REG-1's essence is embedded as in-test watchdog assertions and REG-2 as one REPL test, which mitigates but does not satisfy the merge-rule wording. UT-4 (torn-tail repair) also has no new test — low risk since `session_repair.dart` is untouched and already covered by `test/session/session_repair_test.dart`, but the matrix lists it.
- ⚠️ Late-write sink is not guarded: a throwing `onLateWrite` sink would propagate into the late-write caller, weakening I1's "never thrown into an unhandled zone" (see inline comment on `_sealSessionForExit`).
- 💡 `_reactionRunsSealed` is never reset (latent trap only — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` runs headless exactly once per process and `exit()` follows; see inline comment).
- 💡 Formatting: new test files (and one hunk in `agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) are not `dart format`-clean (see inline comment). No CI format gate exists and the pre-commit hook self-heals, so this is cosmetic.

## Next Steps

1. Land the follow-up card for the REG-1/REG-2 standalone CI jobs + IT-4 + E2E legs before the next TB harness bump, or amend the ticket's merge rule to match the embedded-watchdog reality.
2. Consider wrapping the seal sink call in try/catch so I1's no-throw guarantee holds regardless of sink health.

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # gh-1538: nightly is builds + integration-only now — this PR leg IS the
  # only Terminal-visual run (the nightly cli-visual duplicate is retired).

This is a true seal-contract interaction: boot #1 seals the session on completion, so the post-run `subagentManager.register` (a `shell_job_registry` late write) is now dropped by design (I1) — the te…

blocks.text:
The test: boot #1 runs headless, then registers a zombie subagent row (running) — which the manager persists into the session. Boot #2 runs `runHeadless('hello again')` and expects the zombie row rehydrated from the session and settled to failed/interupted.

With the seal: boot #1's `runHeadless` completes → session sealed. Then `seder.subagentManager.register(...)` persists the registry — but the session is sealed, so the `shell_job_registry` custom-record append is DROPPED. Hence boot #2 rehydrates nothing → handle is null.

This is a genuine design conflict the seal introduced: the PR promises (AC6/I5) "a sealed session resumes normally" and the registry persistence into a sealed session silently drops. The test failure is a true regression of issue #332 behavior in a two-run-same-process scenario.

What's the right fix per the ticket's contract? The ticket says after runHeadless completes the session is sealed — late writes dropped. The test seeds the registry AFTER the headless run completed — a "late write" per the contract, so per I1 the drop is... correct behavior? But the test existed before and encodes a real workflow: the REPL equivalent would allow registering subagents after a run (REPL never ends). In headless, the process would exit right after runHeadless.

Hmm, but is the drop correct? # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

# Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
      FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}'
      FAH_PROVIDER: zai
      FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE: '[{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the

  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.

    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]

  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read

That's actually a cleaner test of "the previous process" — a real previous process would have written its registry rows during its run (pre-seal) or died mid-write. The current test wrote them post-run which is now contractually a dropped late write.

# gh-1589 rework — sealed headless session (CI fix + merge conclusion)

## Issues/Notes

- **CI was red on the merge head `ebb1a7d8`** — three failed checks, one root cause: **Quality gate** (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)` — pure cascade), **Core tests (shard 3/4)**, and **Hostile ambient env** all failed on the SAME test: `test/cli/task_cancel_cli_test.dart` — "headless boot rehydrates the registry (issue #332)" (`Expected: not null / Actual: <null>` — "the registry was rehydrated", line 535). Fetched the failing run's logs via `gh run view 39032714818 --log-failed` since `ci_failures_full.log` was not shipped in `input/`.
- **Root cause — the seal caught a test that encoded the pre-seal world.** The test seeded its zombie `subagent_registry` rows by calling `subagentManager.register/update` **after** `runHeadless` returned. Post-seal, those appends are dropped late writes **by design** (I1: "after the seal, the session JSONL is immutable for this process … late writes are dropped"), so boot #2 rehydrated an empty registry. Production behavior is the contract the ticket specifies; the test's seeding modeled a write the seal now (correctly) forecloses. Verified no production code change was the right call: the registry rehydrate source (`subagentRegistryRows` raw scan) and the seal both behave exactly as specified — only the test's setup was stale. A codebase-wide sweep confirmed this is the only test combining `runHeadless` with post-run registry/board mutations.
- **An `origin/main` merge was left mid-flight by setup** ("All conflicts fixed but you are still merging") — concluded it after verifying every conflicted file resolved to main's side (the branch touches none of the 7).
- The earlier blocked-state notice (thread 13: "no code changes were made") is resolved by this pass's commits.

## Approach

1. Read all refreshed `input/gh-1589/` context (new: `ci_failures.md`, thread 13, raw JSON re-read).
2. Reproduced the CI failure locally first (TDD RED): `dart test test/cli/task_cancel_cli_test.dart -n "runHeadless settles zombie rows"` → identical `Expected: not null / Actual: <null>`.
3. Traced the mechanism: boot #1's `finally` seals the session → the post-run `subagentManager` persists are dropped with one warning per class → boot #2's raw-scan rehydrate finds no `subagent_registry` records.
4. Fixed the test (GREEN) to seed the zombie rows the way a previous process actually leaves them — written **during** its run, before the kill/restart (the ticket's own I4/E2 shape): a fresh `Session` over the same file (E5 — a reopen is unsealed) appends the `subagent_registry` snapshot between the boots. No production change — the seal contract is the point of the PR.
5. Verified the in-progress merge's staged resolution byte-equals main's side for all 7 conflicted files, `git diff --check` clean, concluded the merge (`b7981284db`), committed the test fix (`5c34a8b4dc`).
6. Ran the full non-integration suite under the **exact hostile ambient env** from the CI leg (the red one) as the regression gate.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/task_cancel_cli_test.dart` (+28/−11) — the #332 headless-rehydrate test seeds its zombie registry rows pre-seal through a fresh unsealed Session (E5), modeling the previous process's rows written during its run before dying (I4/E2); comments document why post-run seeding is a dropped late write under the seal (I1).
- Merge commit `b7981284db` — concludes `origin/main` (`3cb7e0e8d7`, gh-1659) into the branch: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/office-addin.yml`, `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart`, `test/ci_1596_installer_portability_ci_test.dart`, `test/ci_1659_office_addin_matrix_test.dart` (new), `test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart`, `test/release_flow_race_test.dart` — all resolved to main's side.

New head: `5c34a8b4dc` on `ai/gh-1589`.

Run on the final head `5c34a8b4dc` (after `dart pub get`):

|---|---|
| `dart test test/cli/task_cancel_cli_test.dart` (the CI-red file) | 7 ✅ (was 1 ❌ before the fix — reproduced RED, then GREEN) |

| `dart analyze test/cli/task_cancel_cli_test.dart` | no issues |
